priceSnapshot.note: The breakdown was a trap. Since the midday snapshot at 63,586.3 price did two distinct things and the second one matters more than the first. That is the second reduce signal to fire on the same calendar day, and it took price through the $1,735,801 shelf at 63,500, the $820,395 shelf at 63,400, the $150,928 shelf at 63,300 and into the $428,173 shelf at 63,200 - four consecutive downside magnets consumed in roughly ninety minutes. Then it reversed. From 63,237.6 price has recovered 588.8 points to 63,826.4, and the recovery has been built on settled closes rather than a wick: 20:00Z at 63,742.3, 01:00Z at 63,828.0 and 02:00Z at 63,756.0. The 01:00Z close is the single most consequential print in this report, because the midday session's add trigger was written as a settled 1H close above 63,800 WITH open interest FALLING across the same bar, and BOTH halves passed. 63,828.0 clears the price half by 28.0 points. Open interest is 2,046,252,459 against the midday read of 2,137,066,952, DOWN 4.25% or $90.8m of notional removed, which clears the inverted open-interest half decisively. That clause was deliberately inverted at midday precisely so it would only pass on short covering rather than on fresh leverage, and it has now done exactly the job it was designed for. Price has also reclaimed the 4H EMA200 at 63,745.48 - the structural floor lost at midday - and sits 80.9 points above it. The counterweight is the calendar: July CPI prints tomorrow at 08:30 ET, which is 07:30 Bogota, forty minutes AFTER the morning session publishes and squarely inside the window this report has to survive.

overnightRisk: The overnight window runs about eleven hours to the 02:00 Bogota midnight session and roughly sixteen hours to the morning report, and it contains one scheduled event that dominates everything else in this file. July CPI is released tomorrow, 12 August, at 08:30 ET - 07:30 Bogota - which is FORTY MINUTES AFTER the 06:50 morning session publishes. Neither the midnight report nor the morning report will have the number; the morning session will be writing into the last minutes of the pre-print vacuum. Consensus is around +0.1% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, and the risk is asymmetric against that consensus because Brent has risen from the low 79s to 89.46 over the past week on the Hormuz stalemate, more than 12% off last week's low, and energy feeds the headline print directly. An upside surprise re-prices rate expectations and hits the highest-beta risk asset first, which on this tape is bitcoin. Three structural conditions make the gap worse than the calendar alone suggests. FIRST, positioning is crowded long: the OKX long/short account ratio is 1.81, having peaked at 1.87 during the recovery, and retail accounts added longs INTO the bounce rather than into the flush. A crowded-long book heading into a binary macro print is the standard precondition for a gap-down cascade. SECOND, the downside liquidity shelf is thin in a specific place. The 18:00-19:00Z sweep consumed 63,500, 63,400, 63,300 and 63,200 - four consecutive magnets - which means those resting orders are gone and there is no realized cluster of any size between 63,200 and the 63,000 handle. A move that clears 63,200 has 200 points of vacuum beneath it. THIRD, the reclaim is only three hours old and rests on a single settled 1H close above 63,800; it has not been retested. Two unscheduled catalysts also sit open: Strategy disclosed a further sale of 1,690 BTC for roughly $109m today and has not signalled that the programme is finished, and the Hormuz negotiation remains live in both directions - a genuine reopening headline would send Brent down hard and bitcoin up, while another escalation does the reverse. The practical consequence is that the resting stop is recommended TRUE this session at 63,380, and it is placed there rather than at the 63,500 reduce level on purpose: 63,500 is the largest realized shelf on the tape and is exactly where a pre-CPI liquidity hunt would wick to, while 63,380 sits beneath the $820,395 shelf at 63,400 and 142.4 points above the swept low of 63,237.6. That gives the position room to survive a shelf test and still exits before the 63,200 vacuum opens. The new spot tranche is deliberately 18 USDT rather than the full 66.89 of dry powder for exactly this reason - the desk wants ammunition on the other side of the print, not exposure into it.

calibration.rollingRecord: Both of the midday session's triggers fired within eight hours of each other, in opposite directions, which has not happened before in this file. The reduce line at 63,400 fired first: the 18:00Z bar settled at 63,372.0, 28.0 points beneath it, and price extended to 63,237.6. Then the add line at 63,800 fired: the 01:00Z bar settled at 63,828.0, 28.0 points above it, and - critically - open interest was falling across that bar, down 4.25% on the session, which cleared the inverted confirmation clause. That clause has now blocked ten would-be entries across eleven sessions and passed exactly once, tonight, which is the behaviour a well-specified filter should show. The reduce record now stands at three fires in nineteen sessions: 64,650 on 10 August morning (honoured, correct), 63,750 today at midday (honoured, then reversed within eight hours), and 63,400 today at endday (fired, immediately reversed). The pattern worth naming is that reduce lines placed at the edge of a swept liquidity zone fire on the sweep itself rather than on a trend, and the two that misfired both did so within a single session of firing.
calibration.note: priorReduceFired is TRUE and actingHelped is FALSE, and the accounting deserves precision because the answer is uncomfortable in one direction and reassuring in another. The midday session moved the decision box to REDUCE and trimmed 25% of the spot core at 63,586.3, honouring a reduce line that had been published for eighteen sessions and had just broken on two consecutive settled hourly closes. That was the correct process. The outcome was poor: price fell a further 348.7 points to 63,237.6 - so the trim did avoid a real drawdown - but then recovered to 63,826.4, which is 240.1 points ABOVE where the trim executed. Marked to now, the trim cost roughly 0.38% on the trimmed notional, or about 16 cents on a 43 USDT sale. So the signal was honoured, the signal was wrong within eight hours, and the cost of being wrong was trivial. That last clause is the point. The desk has now been whipsawed twice in one day - the morning ADD at 64,397.6 was down 1.26% within six hours, and the midday REDUCE at 63,586.3 is down 0.38% within eight - and the combined damage across both is under half a percent of net worth, because both were sized as partials. The reasoning being written to the ledger is not 'stop honouring signals'; it is that in a market whose 15m ATR expanded 92% and then contracted 32% inside twelve hours, signal accuracy collapses while position sizing does all the work. The desk's directional record today is 1 for 3. Its capital preservation record is 3 for 3. Tonight's tranche is sized on the second number, not the first.
